subject: OpenAI-compat migration POC — readout and proposed tests
messages:
From: Nina Patel <nina@acme.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-13T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: Migration compatibility & hyperscaler comparison — next tests

Thanks for the call today — quick recap and ask:

1) Primary goal: validate that switching our inference surface to an OpenAI-compatible API keeps generation parity (prompt/response fidelity) while improving unit cost.
2) Tests we want you to run: prompt-diff report (5 canonical prompts), OpenAI-compat endpoint (chat + completion parity), SDK swap sanity (node + python), latency & token-cost baseline vs GCP Vertex.
3) Targets: 99th perc latency <350ms for 512-token responses; single-request cost delta <= 30% vs our current infra.

I've attached a small prompt suite (acme-prompt-suite.csv) — includes deterministic prompts and a few edge cases (structured JSON outputs, multi-turn context). Procurement needs a short POC plan by 2027-06-20.

Can you confirm owners, what Redwood will run vs what Acme should run, and a lightweight timeline (3–5 business days preferred)?

Thanks,
— Nina
Nina Patel
Sr. ML Engineer, Acme Retail
nina@acme.com
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
To: Nina Patel <nina@acme.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-13T18:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Migration compatibility & hyperscaler comparison — next tests

Hi Nina — great meeting, thanks for the clear asks. Quick readout and proposed plan from our side: 

Summary of what Redwood will deliver (owner in parens):
- Prompt-diff report: run the 5 canonical prompts you attached against Redwood's OpenAI-compat endpoint and a matched Vertex endpoint; report will include tokenized diffs and an automatic quality signal (HED/ROUGE) (Owner: Hannah).
- SDK swap checklist: run simple node/python SDK integration tests (auth, streaming, function-calling, error-handling) against Redwood's compat layer (Owner: Ben).
- Latency & cost baseline: 1000 sample requests across different sequence lengths (64/256/512) to measure p50/p95/p99 latency and token cost; include Dedicated config and Hosted API numbers (Owner: Karthik).
- Compatibility matrix: tabulate any API surface differences and suggested client-side mitigations (Owner: Hannah).

Proposed timeline (all dates in PDT):
- 2027-06-14: small onboarding test (we'll run 50 prompts from your suite) + share redwood-compat-matrix.xlsx (EOD)
- 2027-06-15–16: full batch runs + SDK integration checks
- 2027-06-17: readout deck + prompt-diff report + recommended knobs (quantization profile, batch size, fallback model)

Attachments we'll share now: redwood-compat-matrix.xlsx (compat checklist), mutual-action-plan.docx (minimal MLP for procurement).

Immediate asks for Acme: can you confirm which Vertex SKU (n1-standard vs a2/TPU tiers) you're comparing to, and whether tokenization should follow OpenAI tiktoken standard or your internal tokenizer? That affects prompt-diff fairness.

We'll keep the POC light — if procurement needs something formal we can turn the mutual-action-plan into a short SOW.

Cheers,

Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
hannah@redwood.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>, Nina Patel <nina@acme.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-14T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: OpenAI-compat migration POC — readout and proposed tests

Adding a couple of engineering notes from the SDK/interop angle: 
- For SDK smoke tests we'll cover: streaming chunk boundaries, stop-sequence behavior, role-preserved chat history, and error/retry semantics. If Acme uses our embedded KV cache on multi-turn tests please flag that — behavior differs if you rely on local context assembly.
- Hyperscaler comparison: we'll include runs with and without quantization to show delta in latency and token-cost. Suggest we include two quantization profiles: fp16 (baseline) and 4-bit (production candidate) so Acme can see quality vs unit-price tradeoffs.

I can own the node + python sample repo; will push a minimal github link and a short runbook today.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Staff Engineer, Developer Experience | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai
Attachment: sdk-smoke-runbook.md (stub)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nina Patel <nina@acme.com>
Date: 2027-06-14T10:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: OpenAI-compat migration POC — readout and proposed tests

Operational notes from Dedicated/Hosted side: 
- We'll provision a small Dedicated pool for the POC (2xA10G-equivalent) to show production-like latency. If Acme wants to test burst scenarios we can enable short-duration burst capacity.
- Canary/fallback plan: recommend routing by policy (latency-first) with an automatic fallback to a smaller model variant in the event of 5xx spikes. We'll document the routing policy in the readout.
- I'll need an estimated daily request profile for the POC (rps distribution) to size the run properly — Nina, can you share a 24-hr sample?

I'll coordinate infra and set up dashboards so we can show p50/p99 traces live.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Product Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai
From: Nina Patel <nina@acme.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, procurement@acme.com
Date: 2027-06-14T12:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: OpenAI-compat migration POC — readout and proposed tests

Thanks — this looks good and aligned to what procurement needs. Answers to the immediate asks:
- Vertex SKU: we'll provide runs on n2-highmem and a2-highgpu (we primarily use the a2 family for heavy inference).
- Tokenization: please use OpenAI tiktoken for parity testing; we'll also share a short internal tokenizer snippet if you want to run an apples-to-apples check.
- 24-hr sample RPS: attaching a small telemetry extract (telemetry-sample-24h.csv) — expect ~12 RPS peak, 1–2 RPS typical.

Procurement: procurement@acme.com — we need a short MLP + cost estimate by EOD 2027-06-17. Hannah, can you confirm you'll send that timeline and an estimated cost delta (hosted vs dedicated) in the readout?

I'll wait for the initial 50-prompt run and the compat matrix.

— Nina
Nina Patel
Sr. ML Engineer, Acme Retail
